MINUTES
  Regular Meeting of the
  Gardena City Council
  Tuesday, December 13, 2022

The Regular Meeting Notice and Agenda of the Gardena City Council of the City of Gardena,
California, was called to order at 7:00 PM on Tuesday, December 13, 2022, in the Council
Chamber at City Hall 1700 West 162nd Street, Gardena, California.

1.  ROLL CALL

  Present: Mayor Tasha Cerda; Mayor Pro Tem Paulette C. Francis; Council Member Mark
  E. Henderson; Council Member Rodney G. Tanaka; and Council Member Wanda Love;
  Other City Officials and Employees present: City Treasurer Guy H. Mato; City Manager
  Clint Osorio; City Attorney Carmen Vasquez; and City Clerk Mina Semenza.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION - None

2.  CLOSED SESSION

  2.A  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL- EXISTING LITIGATION
  Gov. Code Section 54956.9(d)(1)
  Zoila Monroy, Aragon; Genesis Dubon; and Kelly Dubon v. City of Gardena, et
  al. L.A. Sup. Ct. Case No.: 20STCV46821

  Mayor Cerda announced the cancellation of Closed Session.

CITY ATTORNEY REPORT OUT OF CLOSED SESSION - None

3.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Neil Hance and Savannah Hance led the Pledge of Allegiance. Both attend Amestoy
  Elementary School. Neil and Savannah were selected as pledgers because they are
  model students who show leadership abilities and always strive to do their best at
  Amestoy Elementary School. In addition, their mom is very involved in their school and
  serves as the Secretary of School Site Council. Assistant Principal, Dr. Elda Pech,
  accompanied them to the meeting.

4.  INVOCATION

  Reverend Scott R. Fairchild, of CrossRoad Church, gave the Invocation.

5.  PRESENTATIONS

  5.A  Senator Steven Bradford - Legislative Update - Senator Steven Bradford,
  Representing the 35th District gave his introduction and updates on this
  year's Budget Investments for Californians, his Budget Accomplishments
  and 2022 Legislation.

  Council Member Love and Mayor Pro Tem Francis thanked Senator Bradford on
  behalf of the City of Gardena.

  1
   5.B  Certificates of Commendation in Special Recognition of Retirements and Long
  Time Service to the City of Gardena:
  (a) Juan Bareno, Sewer Maintenance Worker- 21.8 years - (Public Works)
  - Director of Public Works, Allan Riggs introduced Juan Bareno, Sewer
  Maintenance Worker. Mr. Bareno was present and accepted his certificate
  and recognition.

  5.C  2022 Most Business-Friendly City Award
  - Economic Development Manager, Jackie Cho presented a PowerPoint
  presentation capturing photos of our city officials accepting the award.

  Mayor Cerda showed the award and thanked Jackie and all departments, who
  participated in making it a reality.

6.  PROCLAMATIONS - None

7.  APPOINTMENTS

  7.A  Gardena Rent Mediation Board - Member at Large - Woods Woolwine
  - was Appointed by Mayor Cerda

  Mr. Woolwine expressed his appreciation and thanked all Members of the
  Council for the appointment.

  It was moved by Mayor Cerda, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Francis, and
  carried by the following roll call vote to Appoint Woods Woolwine to the
  Gardena Rent Mediation Board – Member at Large:

  Ayes:  Mayor Cerda, Mayor Pro Tem Francis, and Council Members
  Henderson, Tanaka, and Love
  Noes:  None
  Absent: None

8.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  8.A  Waiver of Reading in Full of All Ordinances Listed on This Agenda and that they Be
  read by Title Only
  CONTACT: CITY CLERK

  8.B  Approve Minutes:
  Regular Meeting of the City Council, November 8, 2022
  CONTACT: CITY CLERK

  8.C  Receive and File of Minutes:
  Planning & Environmental Quality Commission, July 19, 2022
  Planning & Environmental Quality Commission, September 6, 2022
  Planning & Environmental Quality Commission, November 1, 2022
  CONTACT: COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT

  2
   8.D  Approval of Warrants/Payroll Register, November 22, 2022
  CONTACT: CITY TREASURER

  November 22, 2022: Wire Transfer: 12267-12272; Prepay: 169619-169622; Check
  Nos: 169623-169779 – for a total Warrants issued in the amount of $2,400,983.60;
  Total Payroll Issued for November 18, 2022: $2,117,609.98.

  8.E  Approval of Warrants/Payroll Register, December 13, 2022
  CONTACT: CITY TREASURER

  December 13, 2022: Wire Transfer: 12273-12284; Prepay: 169780-169789; Check
  Nos: 169790 -169976 – for a total Warrants issued in the amount of $3,062,609.66;
  Total Payroll Issued for December 2, 2022: $1,673,945.44.

  8.F  Monthly Investment Report, October 2022
  CONTACT: CITY TREASURER

  8.G  Personnel Report P-2022-21 12-13-22
  CONTACT: HUMAN RESOURCES

  8.H  Authorize Agreement between South Bay Workforce Investment Board, Inc., on
  behalf of the City of Inglewood, and the City of Gardena through June 30, 2024
  CONTACT: ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES

  8.I  Acceptance and Notice of Completion for the Gardena Community Aquatic and
  Senior Center Project - Demolition Phase, JN 978
  CONTRACT: PUBLIC WORKS

  It was moved by Council Member Tanaka, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem
  Francis, and carried by the following roll call vote to Approve all Items on the
  Consent Calendar:

  Ayes:  Council Member Tanaka, Mayor Pro Tem Francis, Council Members
  Henderson and Love, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes:  None
  Absent: None

9.  EXCLUDED CONSENT CALENDAR- None

10. PLANNING & ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY COMMISSION ACTION SHEET

  10.A NOVEMBER 15, 2022 MEETING - Meeting Cancelled

  10.B DECEMBER 6, 2022 MEETING

  2022 Planning Commission Recap

  Staff presented to the Planning Commission a recap of the past development and
  planning policy project that went before the Commission over the past year.

  Commission Action: No action taken.

  City Council: No action needed

  3
 11. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

  1) Andrea Simental – Manager of Masao Library; came to announce library events for
  Masao W. Satow Library.

  2) Brandon Smith - made a request for bike lanes on Vermont Ave - adding a bike lane to
  that road will help with the revitalization of Gardena Blvd.

  3) City Clerk Mina Semenza, noted for the record that two emails were received from the
  public stating that they have been forwarded to the City Council, and are available for
  viewing at the City Clerk’s office

12. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES

  12.A City of Gardena Audit Reports for Fiscal Year Ended June 30, 2022: Annual
  Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR), Family Child Care and GTrans

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report and gave a PowerPoint
  presentation. Director of Administrative Services Ray Beeman was present and
  assisted with the presentation.

  City Manager Osorio introduced Sophia Kuo of The Pun Group. She thanked City
  Manager Osorio, Director Ray Beeman and staff for all their help.

  Council Member Henderson asked since we have gone so far over our projected
  reserve how do we get control of it; could you further clarify what the Pension
  Obligation Bond is and explain we did not use this money to fund our pension. City
  Manager Osorio explained what the Pension Obligation Bond is and how it works.

  Council Member Tanaka asked how much does it cost a month to run the city? Did
  other cities try to do a Pension Obligation Bond like we did but were too late? City
  Manager explained in detail and answered all questions.

  This Item was Received and Filed Audit Reports for Fiscal Year 2021-2022

  12.B Approve Microsoft Software Assurance and Licensing Agreement with Dell
  Technologies for $575,787.12 for the period January 1, 2023, thru December 31,
  2025.

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  Public Speaker: Zahid Ahmed, spoke and suggested creating a computer lab at
  Rowley Park; to increase the number of licenses and expand upon the contract;
  making it kind of like a college career center for students of all ages; it is certainly
  needed in our city.

  Mayor Cerda asked if the licenses are for city staff. City Manager Osorio confirmed
  yes, that it is for 492 licenses.

  4
   It was moved by Council Member Henderson, seconded by Council Member
  Tanaka, and carried by the following roll call vote to Approve Proposal:

  Ayes:  Council Members Henderson and Tanaka, Mayor Pro Tem Francis,
  Council Member Love, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes:  None
  Absent: None

13. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT

  13.A New Fortunetelling Permit - #2 Psychic Reading & Meditation Center 1602 Artesia
  Boulevard Unit F Gardena, California 90248

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  Mayor Cerda asked if the Applicant was here. No one came up. Mayor Cerda then
  asked how long the business was operating without a business license before they
  were cited. Director of Community Development Greg Tsuijuchi answered her
  question.

  It was moved by Council Member Henderson, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem
  Francis, and carried by the following roll call vote to Approve a New
  Fortunetelling Permit for Sophie Adams and Tiffany D. Johnson (dba: #2
  Psychic Reading & Mediation Center):

  Ayes:  Council Member Henderson, Mayor Pro Tem Francis, Council
  Members Tanaka and Love, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes:  None
  Absent: None

  13.B ORDINANCE NO. 1846, Relating to the Protection of Property During Demolition,
  Including a Determination that the Ordinance is Exempt from the Provisions of the
  California Environmental Quality Act Pursuant to the Common Sense Exemption
  Set Forth in Guidelines Section 15061(B)(3) and Under CEQA Guidelines Section
  15305 (Class 5) for Minor Alterations in Land Use Limitations

  ORDINANCE NO.1846

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  GARDENA, CALIFORNIA, ADDING CHAPTER 15.52 TO TITLE
  15, BUILDINGS AND CONSTRUCTION, OF THE GARDENA
  MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO THE PROTECTION OF
  PROPERTY DURING DEMOLITION

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  Mayor Pro Tem Francis asked if there was a size limitation that would trigger the
  guidelines of this ordinance; and who is responsible for regulating the ordinance?
  Director of Community Development, Greg Tsuijuchi, came up and answered her
  questions and explained the procedure, and laws that are in place.

  5
   Ordinance No. 1846 was Introduced by Council Member Tanaka

  It was moved by Council Member Love, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Francis,
  and carried by the following roll call vote to Introduce Ordinance No. 1846:

  Ayes:  Council Member Love, Mayor Pro Tem Francis, Council Members
  Henderson and Tanaka, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes:  None
  Absent: None

14. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - ELECTED & CITY MANAGER'S OFFICES

  14.A COVID-19 Update - City Manager Osorio provided the update.

15. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS – POLICE

  15.A  Notification of Eligibility for Funding in the amount of $123,276.00 Under the
  Tobacco Grant Program Award for the 2022 - 2023 Grant Cycle

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  Council Member Tanaka asked if this was going to include flavored tobacco
  products.

  Mayor Pro Tem Francis asked if vaping was included? Where are the retail checks
  being done: gas stations; convenience stores? What about tobacco stores and is it
  for school age children?

  Chief of Police Mike Saffell came up and answered all of their questions.

  It was moved by Council Member Love, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Francis,
  and carried by the following roll call vote to Accept Grant Award and
  Authorize Expenditures:

  Ayes:  Council Member Love, Mayor Pro Tem Francis, Council Members
  Henderson and Tanaka, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes:  None
  Absent: None

  15.B Authorization to Award a Two-Year Video Policing System Camera Maintenance
  and Repair Contract to DataGear, Inc. in the Amount Not to Exceed $133,902.40.

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  Public Speaker: Zahid Ahmed, spoke about having a backup server to back up all
  the data and possibly getting shot spotter software and offered other
  recommendations for using this software; also suggested using Google for camera
  video surveillance.

  6
   Mayor Pro Tem Francis asked if this was a renewal or a brand-new contract? City
  Manager Osorio replied to her question.

  Mayor Cerda asked about the recommendations that were suggested by the Public
  Speaker, asking if those could be applied to this software. Chief Saffell answered
  all questions.

  It was moved by Council Member Tanaka, seconded by Council Member
  Henderson, and carried by the following roll call vote to Authorize and
  execute a two-year contract, with optional one-year extension, for the Video
  Policing System Camera Maintenance and Repair to DataGear, Inc:

  Ayes:  Council Members Tanaka and Henderson, Mayor Pro Tem Francis,
  Council Member Love, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes:  None
  Absent: None

16. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - PUBLIC WORKS

  16.A Award Construction Management and Inspection Services Contract for the
  Gardena Community Aquatic and Senior Center Project, JN 978, to Griffin
  Structures, Inc., in the amount of $895,000.

  Council Member Tanaka recused himself and left the dais for this item.

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  Public Speaker: Zahid Ahmed spoke and suggested trying to cap the change
  orders based on a longer period of time and if some of the money could be used
  towards another project in the City.

  Public Works Director Allan Rigg came up and explained the process.

  Mayor Pro Tem Francis asked the following: since we have multiple projects that
  are similar to this, can we hire a person to take care of it all. She then stated that
  your loyalty is to who takes care of you and getting the job done and she wants to
  make sure that we are adequately staffed particularly in Public Works, we keep
  hiring consultants; she then asked if we can forsee projects in the future and have
  this person work on those projects as well. She then asked that your anticipating
  that your department will never be fully staffed is that what your are suggesting?

  City Manager Osorio stated that it is more cost effective to hire each time when the
  project ends. Director of Public Works Allan Rigg answered all questions and
  explained the process and benefit of hiring consultants.

  Mayor Cerda asked, overall, for the day to day tasks; we have adequate staff?

  Council Member Love asked if it is possible for us to use this consultant for the
  Rosecrans Chase project since its similar to the aquatic center project?

  7
   Director Rigg answered all questions.

  It was moved by Council Member Love, seconded by Council Member
  Henderson, and carried by the following roll call vote to Award Construction
  Management and Inspection Services Contract:

  Ayes:  Council Members Love and Henderson, Mayor Pro Tem Francis, and
  Mayor Cerda
  Noes: None
  Absent: None
  Abstain: Council Member Tanaka

Mayor Cerda took this Item Out of Order.

16.D Authorize Payments to Southern California Edison in the amount of $69,439.10 and
  AT&T in the amount of $26,443.23 to Underground the Existing Overhead Utilities
  for the Gardena Community Aquatic and Senior Center Project, JN 978

  Council Member Tanaka recused himself and left the dais for this item.

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  City Manager Osorio noted that the amount of $26,443.23 will no longer be
  needed, due to the negotiation done by Assistant Public Works Director, Kevin
  Kwak.

  Council Member Henderson thanked Mr. Kwak and commented looking at the
  aesthetics can we develop a plan to start working on an underground utility; or
  possibly looking at our commercial corridors? Public Works Director Allan Rigg
  replied and explained that is something we can definitely look into.

  It was moved by Council Member Henderson, seconded by Council Member
  Love, and carried by the following roll call vote to Authorize Payment to
  Utility Companies:

  Ayes:  Council Members Henderson and Love, Mayor Pro Tem Francis, and
  Mayor Cerda
  Noes:  None
  Absent: None
  Abstain: Council Member Tanaka

16.B Award Construction Contract for the New Marked Crosswalk with Pedestrian Hybrid
  Beacon on Vermont Avenue and 133rd Street, JN 972 to California Professional
  Engineering, Inc. in the amount of $314,488. Approve the Project Plans &
  Specifications, Approve Budget Appropriation of $250,000 funds, and Declare
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Exemption.

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  Public Works Director Allan Rigg presented a couple of graphics of what the light
  would look like. He then stated that basically what you’re approving is a pedestrian
  active stop light.

  8
   Mayor Cerda asked about the type of light and if there was going to be any type of
  public outreach.

  Mayor Pro Tem Francis asked if this was going to go all the way across Vermont,
  what about the median? She then asked why not put in a regular traffic light?

  Council Member Henderson asked about the data collected and suggested putting
  a similar light on Western to 147th Street.

  Council Member Love asked if it will be an audio light? Will the red light go on first if
  you have a person with a disability?

  Mayor Cerda asked if you have the number of accidents at this location. And asked
  the length of the study period?

  Director Rigg answered all questions.

  It was moved by Council Member Love, seconded by Mayor Cerda, and
  carried by the following roll call vote to Award Construction Contract,
  Approve Project Plans and Specifications, Approve Budget Appropriation
  and Contingency and Declare CEQA Exemption:

  Ayes:  Council Member Love, Mayor Cerda, Mayor Pro Tem Francis, and
  Council Members Henderson and Tanaka
  Noes: None
  Absent: None

16.C Award Professional Design Services Contract for the Mas Fukai Park
  Improvements Project, JN 820, to David Volz Design Landscape Architects, Inc., in
  the amount of $755,830.

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  Council Member Henderson asked about the renovated irrigation system, and does
  it include storm water capture?

  Mayor Pro Tem Francis asked if the funding source is Park-in-Lieu and will it be
  cost effective to get recycled water?

  Council Member Love asked if we could look into seeing the cost of underground
  water storage; I understand it’s expensive but is it worth the cost. She continued to
  say that if we could partner with West Basin and Met Water to see if there is any
  funding available.

  Mayor Cerda commented on the recycled water at Johnson Park, at the time, we
  thought there was not going be any expense to us, but City ending up putting
  money in for the piping; she then asked if there would be an additional cost to us if
  we went with underground water storage.

  Director of Public Works Allan Rigg answered all questions.

  9
   It was moved by Council Member Love, seconded by Council Member
  Tanaka, and carried by the following roll call vote to Approve Professional
  Services Contract:

  Ayes:  Council Members Love and Tanaka, Mayor Pro Tem Francis, Council
  Member Henderson, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes: None
  Absent: None

  16.E Award Construction Contract for Manhattan Beach Blvd. Drought Tolerant
  Landscape Conversion Maintenance Project to Venco Western Inc. In The Amount
  Of $46,279.00; Additionally Declare CEQA Exemption and Approve Project Plans

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  Public Speaker: Zahid Ahmed, spoke and gave his recommendations for all of the
  medians in Gardena that these services could be applied.

  Mayor Cerda asked how did we come up with that location?

  Mayor Pro Tem Francis asked about a previous award of contract to Mariposa
  Landscaping. She then asked why we have to have an additional contract.

  Public Works Director Allan Rigg explained it was for a different scope of work and
  answered all questions.

  It was moved by Council Member Love, seconded by Council Member
  Tanaka, and carried by the following roll call vote to Award Construction
  Project, Approve Project Plans and Declare CEQA Exemption:

  Ayes:  Council Members Love and Tanaka, Council Member Henderson,
  and Mayor Cerda
  Noes:  Mayor Pro Tem Francis
  Absent: None

17. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - RECREATION & HUMAN SERVICES - No Items

18. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS – TRANSPORTATION - No Items

19. COUNCIL ITEMS - No Items

20. COUNCIL DIRECTIVES

  Council Member Henderson

  1) Asked City Manager if we could send a letter to the National Civic League so the City
  could participate for the “All American City” award; deadline for letter submission is 1
  2/15/2022 – was seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Francis

  2) Asked City Manager if we could look into participating in the National League of Cities’
  grant application bootcamp; he understands that they have grant funding available to
  address the Brownsfield sites in our City – was seconded by Mayor Pro Tem
  Francis

  10
   Mayor Pro Tem Francis

  1) Asked staff to do a study, and research if storage units are needed for our Recreation
  Department to store items that are used at City events; if the study shows that storage
  units are needed, then please provide the costs – was seconded by Council
  Member Love

  Council Member Love

  1) Asked if staff could look into adding some type of lighting to the bus stop area near the
  Dollar Tree; the bus stop is underneath a tree and is very dark, which makes it unsafe
  at night – was seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Francis

21. CITY MANAGER REMARKS RE: DIRECTIVES / COUNCIL ITEMS

  1) Video presentation highlighting the Recreation and Human Services Department
  current and future events.

22. COUNCIL REMARKS

  1) MAYOR PRO TEM FRANCIS – Mayor Pro Tem Francis is proud of all the
  accomplishments and proud of staff. Since the last meeting Mayor Pro Tem Francis
  attended the CERT holiday potluck, GTRANS awards banquet, Helping Hands Toy
  giveaway, City staff holiday party, Greater Los Angeles Vector Control District meeting,
  and Winter Wonderland. Mayor Pro Tem Francis encouraged everyone to celebrate
  their traditions, enjoy, and have a lot of fun. She also shared Christmas is about
  spending time with families and friends. She wishes everyone to eat a lot, be healthy,
  and be happy.

  2) COUNCIL MEMBER TANAKA – Council Member Tanaka thanked Director Santin for
  all the events they attended. Council Member Tanaka attended the Eddy Awards and
  congratulated staff and the city on the 1st place award for Most Business-Friendly City.
  Since the last meeting Council Member Tanaka attended the swearing-in ceremony for
  Commissioner Kale, Veterans dinner at the Elks, 53rd Veterans Day remembrance at
  City Hall, Toshio Hirai Memorial, SBCOG open house, catalytic converter etching
  event, Wobble before you Gobble, Coop and fire grand opening, Village Mobile Home
  Park annual friends sharing luncheon, holiday trolley at Freeman Park, Finance
  Committee meeting, and CERT annual business meeting. Council Member Tanaka
  also participated in the memorial for Rich Fujio and shared his daughter Kelly was part
  of the city staff and Mr. Fujio was a contributor to making the City of Gardena a great
  place. He also attended the Helping Hands giveaway, City staff Christmas celebration,
  Winter Wonderland, and Kiwanis Club lunch for the seniors. Council Member Tanaka
  apologized to Director Crespo for missing the GTrans holiday party. Lastly, shared he
  appreciates staff for their hard work and the City of Gardena is the gem of the South
  Bay. Wished everyone a Merry Christmas, Happy Kwanzaa, Happy Hanukkah, Feliz
  Navidad, and wishes the year 2023 will be great year for everyone.

  11
   3) COUNCIL MEMBER LOVE – Since the last meeting Council Member Love attended
  the Eddy Awards, Veterans Day Memorial, turkey giveaway with the Chamber, jolly
  trolley to Freeman Park, joint job fair with the South Bay Workforce Investment Board,
  jolly trolley to Johnson Park, Brotherhood Crusade Honorary Mookie Betts, breakfast
  with Santa Claus, MLK and fashion show, Winter Wonderland, and golf tournament in
  Calabasas. During the upcoming weekend the Chamber will be giving a toy grab and
  go for anyone in the community and on Christmas Day the Chamber will be hosting a
  lunch to feed anyone in city that may need a meal. Council Member Love recognized
  Mrs. Williams for attending the meeting and expressed her sympathy to her and her
  family on the loss of her son Ronald B. Williams.

  4) MAYOR CERDA – Since the last meeting Mayor Cerda attended the Eddy Awards and
  Passport to Wellness event thanked Officer Kim and all the organizations that
  participated. She also attended the Elks Veterans appreciation dinner, Veterans Day
  ceremony, retirement party for a resident Michelle Benjamin, GTrans anniversary for
  the 110 express lane press conference at the Harbor Gateway, Toshio Hirai Memorial,
  monthly CCGA meeting, Sanitation meeting, LA County City Selection meeting for the
  Southwest Corridor, Casino Night, catalytic converter etching event, Wobble before
  you Gobble, grand opening of Coop and Fire, Village Mobile Homes holiday party,
  CERT graduating class for 2022, 15th annual Thanksgiving dinner at Pollo Inka, Coffee
  with a Cop, community meeting for 129th and Western, home owners meeting, GTrans
  award celebration, Second Time Around Club insulation on Monday, and top-notch
  volunteers dinner. Mayor Cerda thanked city departments for working together to have
  the jolly trolley event. She also attended the Finance Committee meeting, Tri-City
  CERT annual Christmas potluck, swearing in of the president for the LA Southwest
  Realtors Association which is her sister, Helping Hands toy giveaway, SURF toy and
  turkey giveaway, Winter Wonderland, Kiwanis lunch, swearing in of Mark Warnick
  through the South Bay Association of Chambers of Commerce. Mayor Cerda thanked
  all the employees for their great job throughout the entire year and shared employees
  reflect Council.

  5) COUNCIL MEMBER HENDERSON – Council Member Henderson expressed his
  happy holidays wishes to everyone. Council Member Henderson shared a story that
  occurred at the CERT Tri-City Dinner, he had the opportunity to sit with the Parks and
  Recreation Director, Chief of Police, and Community Development Director and so they
  had a conversation of leadership and management styles. From the conversation
  Council Member Henderson understood that the cities leadership is thoughtful,
  empathetic, strategic, proactive, and always looking to do things different.
  Acknowledged that Directors are working hard and developing staff to do more. Also
  acknowledge City Manager Osorio, City Clerk, and City Attorney Vasquez. Lastly,
  Council Member Henderson is looking forward to the new year.

23. ANNOUNCEMENT(S) - None

  12
 24. REMEMBRANCES

  Mr. Ronald B. Williams, long time Gardena resident since 1973. He attended local
  Gardena schools and graduated from Gardena High School. Mr. Williams attended UC
  San Diego and graduated in 1992, he then attended Cal State Dominguez Hills where he
  earned his teaching credential and MA. In 2005, Mr. Williams began teaching Secondary
  World History and 9th grade Life Skills at Gardena High School, where he also assisted
  with coaching and mentoring the students of Gardena High School. After two years of
  classroom teaching , Mr. Williams became the Dean of Discipline from 2006-201 1. Mr.
  Williams made it his personal mission to support students and parents at every
  opportunity and treated all students and their families with fairness and dignity. He will be
  greatly missed; Mr. Dwayne Nathaniel Battle, 60 years of age and longtime Gardena
  resident since 1968. Mr. Battle attended Purche Avenue Elementary and Maria Regina
  Elementary School. He graduated from Gardena High School in 1980; Mr. Richard
  Shigeru Fujio, 83 years of age. Mr. Fujio was a pillar of our City. He was a successful
  businessman, gracious & generous volunteer, and loving family man. He owned and
  operated "Rich's Carpet" in Gardena for 40 years. He was a stalwart member of the
  Gardena Kiwanis Club, donating tens of thousands of dollars to worthy community
  causes. Mr. Fujio is survived by his daughter Kelly, son Rich, his sister in Chicago,
  brother in La Quinta, sister and brother-in-law in Gardena, and many nieces and
  nephews. He will be greatly missed.

25. ADJOURNMENT

  At 11 :15 p.m., Mayor Cerda stated that the December 27, 2022 Gardena City Council
  Meeting was cancelled and adjourned the Gardena City Council Meeting to the Closed
  Session portion of the City Council Meeting at 7:00 p.m., and the Regular City Council
  Meeting at 7:30 p.m. on Tuesday, January 10, 2023.

  MINA SEMENZA
  City Clerk of the City of Gardena and
  Ex-officio Clerk of the Council
APPROVED:

~~
~Cerda, Mayor
  By & ~ ~
  Becky Romero, Deputy City Clerk

  13
